newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares rebound on macroeconomic data.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares rebound on macroeconomic data.

text.p: Hungarian share prices bounced back on Thursday on what traders attributed to the beneficial impact of the most recent macroeconomic figures.
The BUX index closed at 3,616.49 points, up 30.72.
"I think this was due to the relatively good macroeonomic figures released yesterday and today," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities. "These macroeconomic data triggered price increases."
"Price rises were not very significant but they may mark the beginning of a modestly bullish trend," Agoston said.
The strengthening of Hungary's Purchasing Manager Index to 60.4 percent in September from 52.7 percent in August was also encouraging, he said.
Traders expected the pharmaceutical shares and hotel firm Danubius to be the main beneficiaries of the rising trend on the bourse.
Oil and gas company MOL 's shares firmed 30 points to end at 1,630 in lively trade.
Packaging firm Cofinec strengthened 190 forints or 4.41 percent to end at 4,500.
Chemical company Borsodchem regained Wednesday's 40 forint loss and ended at 3,000 forints, up 40.
